item.title: Fabry-P\'erot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
item.description: arXiv:2611.00178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-P\'erot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Kumar, Yat-Yin Au, Snorri Ingvarsson

item.title: A Julia implementation of Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation in periodic systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.00354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a flexible Julia codebase implementing Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation (HHG) in periodic tight-binding systems. Using the frequency-domain Fourier-Sambe formalism, the package maps the time-dependent Schroedinger equation onto a static eigenvalue problem. This allows direct computation of Floquet states, quasienergy bands, and harmonic currents for 1D, 2D, or 3D lattices under arbitrary light polarizations. The implementation supports both analytical Fourier-Bessel expansions (via Peierls substitution) and numerical Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). We validate the code against a canonical 1D two-band model and showcase its capabilities on 2D honeycomb systems: gapped graphene mapping HHG cutoff scaling with hopping parameters and the Kane-Mele model, exploring field-induced quasienergy gaps and topological transitions under linear and circular driving fields. In addition to the theoretical presentation, we provide a flexible and efficient open-source Julia implementation of the Floquet formalism: https://github.com/Ashwin-A-Pillai/Floquet-Fourier-Numericals/tree/main.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Pillai, Aurelien Manchon, Claudio Attaccalite

item.title: Zeeman Spin Photocurrents without Spin Textures
item.description: arXiv:2611.00655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inversion symmetry forbids bulk second-order spin photocurrents driven solely by electric-dipole coupling. We show that interference between the electric-dipole and spin Zeeman couplings of light enables Zeeman spin-shift and spin-injection currents in centrosymmetric magnets. Our microscopic theory and systematic symmetry analysis establish the allowed responses and polarization selection rules for both spin-degenerate and spin-split antiferromagnets, with and without spin--orbit coupling (SOC). In collinear magnets without SOC, spin injection vanishes, whereas a pure spin-shift current survives independently of the carrier scattering time. This response arises from transverse electronic spin coherences generated by the optical magnetic field, while the ordered moments remain collinear and fixed. Model analyses validate the mechanism, and first-principles calculations for $\mathrm{MnF_2}$ predict experimentally accessible spin photocurrents. These findings establish a general framework for optical spin-current generation in centrosymmetric magnets, including a SOC-free pure-spin mechanism particularly relevant to altermagnets.
item.dc:creator: Xihua Xiao, Ruizhi Dong, Ruixiang Fei

item.title: Anomalous response, re-emerging localization-transition and robust corner sates in self-similar peano fractal
item.description: arXiv:2611.01099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anomalous spectral response from the non-interacting electrons on a peano fractal is recorded within tight-binding framework. It is observed that a minimal off-diagonal anisotropy can modulate the transport characteristics of the lattice. Drastic modification in the nature of the eigenstates has been validated through the workout of level spacing statistics. Further, a two-dimensional quasiperiodic Aubry-Andr\'e and Harper variation in the overlap integral can invite re-entrant localization-delocalization transition for the self-similar model. This is associated with the possible existence of single-particle mobility edge in the energy landscape. Our results are corroborated by the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, fractal dimension and quantum dynamical response. The spectrum is shown to formulate a quantum butterfly pattern with the frequency of the modulation. Chiral symmetry protected edge states are found to be insensitive with respect to moderate diagonal disorder.
item.dc:creator: Rhiddha Acharjee (Department of Physics, University of Calcutta, 92, Acharya Prafulla Chandra Road, Kolkata, West Bengal-700009, India), Sayan Bhattacharya (Department of Physics, Acharya Prafulla Chandra College, New Barrackpore, Kolkata, West Bengal-700131, India), Atanu Nandy (Department of Physics, Acharya Prafulla Chandra College, New Barrackpore, Kolkata, West Bengal-700131, India), Debnarayan Jana (Department of Physics, University of Calcutta, 92, Acharya Prafulla Chandra Road, Kolkata, West Bengal-700009, India)

item.title: Galilean electrodynamics fluctuation in a superfluid: from general coordinate invariance to Tkachenko mode
item.description: arXiv:2611.02482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore coupling the Galilean electrodynamics (GED) to an s-wave superfluid. Governed by the general coordinate invariance, the proposed effective Lagrangian hosts an unconventional superfluid whose mass is shifted by the GED gauge multiplet. We compute its electromagnetic and gravitational responses in the linear regime. In the long-wavelength limit, we discover a vanishing pressure response, and remarkably the collective mode assumes a quadratic dispersion relation reminiscent of the Tkachenko mode in an oscillating vortex lattice in (2+1) dimensions. We further demonstrate that the soft sector of the vortex lattice model is a GED in disguise, and illustrate the relation between the gauge multiplet and the Lifshitz scalar in the lowest-Landau-level regime of the vortex lattice.
item.dc:creator: Neng-Chun Chiu, Tzu-Ken Shen, Siau Ihan

item.title: Synchronization and Spatiotemporal Phases in Driven Precessing Domain Walls
item.description: arXiv:2611.03110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The dynamics of extended magnetic domain walls driven by constant and alternating magnetic fields are studied using a collective coordinate $u$-$\phi$ model. While purely constant-field driven systems exhibit deterministic spatiotemporal chaos and roughening, the alternating component can lock the precessional frequency via Shapiro-like steps. Using linear stability analysis and Floquet theory, the phase boundaries of stable, synchronized flat wall states are mapped. By studying the nonlinear dynamics of the extended system, a rich phase diagram is identified, composed of five dynamical regimes characterized by the combination of domain wall spatial order (flat, rough, or periodic) and domain wall precession temporal order (pinned, synchronized, or unsynchronized). Notably, the macroscopic temporal order of the synchronized phases can lead to a flat domain wall or to a periodic structure dominated by a narrow band of linearly unstable modes, both with coherent precession of the domain wall magnetization, while unsynchronized phases can be flat, with coherent precession, or rough with spatiotemporal chaos and incoherent precession.
item.dc:creator: Luz P\'erez Herrera, Enzo Fabrizio Pusiol, Alejandro B. Kolton

item.title: Quantum Dipolar Magnon Drag in Conducting Magnetic Bilayers
item.description: arXiv:2611.00320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We predict electrical drag between two electrically isolated metallic ferromagnets mediated by quantum dipolar magnon coupling. A charge current in one layer generates a nonequilibrium magnon current whose momentum is transferred across an insulating spacer through interlayer dipolar interactions. The resulting magnon current in the passive layer produces a measurable voltage through electron-magnon scattering. We show the combination of resonant quantum momentum transfer and magnetic tunability through the control of magnetization configurations distinguish quantum dipolar drag from conventional drag mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Ling Gan, Shufeng Zhang

item.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.01110v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter $\alpha$ deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding $W_0(\alpha)=\pm1$, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases $\alpha$ where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.
item.dc:creator: Daksh K. Sambhare, Koustav Roy, Saurabh Basu

item.title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.01697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $\mu$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.
item.dc:creator: Ganga S. Kumar, Kusumpal Yadav, Miral Verma, Parushottam Majhi, Pragati Sharma, Kaustuv Chatterjee, Sandip Bysakh, Sudipta Goswami, Prabir Pal, Chandan K. Ghosh, S. B. Roy, Vasant Sathe, Devajyoti Mukherjee, Dipten Bhattacharya

item.title: When Does Triadic Balance Reduce to Pairwise Order?
item.description: arXiv:2611.02117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Structural-balance interactions are naturally defined on triads, but when pair affinities are themselves generated by continuous node attributes, it is not clear whether the resulting interaction remains genuinely higher order. Here we address this question for agents represented by unit vectors in an attribute space, with pair affinity given by their scalar product and a Heider product assigned to each triangle. For planar attributes, we show that the triadic interaction reduces exactly, at finite system size, to a pairwise Curie--Weiss XY model of the doubled angles. The ordered phase is therefore nematic and undergoes a continuous mean-field $O(2)$ transition at $k_{\mathrm B}T_c=J/8$. The same reduction reveals a local $\mathbb Z_2$ degeneracy: each nematically ordered state corresponds to $2^N$ polar assignments, whose binomial multiplicities make two nearly equal opposite groups typical at low temperature. Monte Carlo simulations support the exact critical temperature, the mean-field Binder-cumulant value, and the predicted complete-graph finite-size scaling. Finally, a tensor representation of the interaction shows that the planar reduction is dimension specific: in two dimensions the cubic invariant is constrained by lower-order invariants, whereas for $d\geq3$ it is generically independent. These results identify when attribute-induced triadic balance is effectively pairwise and when genuinely higher-order structure can remain.
item.dc:creator: Sepideh Arab Mohammadi, Amir Kargaran, Ali Hosseiny, Reza Jafari, Abbas Ali Saberi

item.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.02351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 {\mu}s and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: F. Mahdikhany, J. Cutshall, et al., Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure, Physical Review B 114, 105307 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Fateme Mahdikhany, Jacob Cutshall, Daniel Shanks, Garett Reichenbach, Davoud Adinehloo, Michael R. Koehler, David G. Mandrus, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Vasili Perebeinos, Brian J. LeRoy, John R. Schaibley

item.title: Chiral phonon magnetism from localized Raman excitation
item.description: arXiv:2611.02594v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal {\alpha}-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.
item.dc:creator: Yuhan Wang, Chuanshan Tian

item.title: Polariton tweezers
item.description: arXiv:2611.03506v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.
item.dc:creator: Nika Gribova, Evgeny Sedov, Alexey Kavokin

item.title: Multiple windows of eigenstate-selective delocalization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice
item.description: arXiv:2611.03562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate localization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice with a real quasiperiodic onsite potential of strength $W$ and a staggered imaginary quasiperiodic modulation of strength $\lambda$. Using the inverse participation ratio (IPR), normalized participation ratio (NPR), fractal dimension $D_2$, transfer-matrix Lyapunov exponent, and wave-packet dynamics, we find a strongly non-monotonic and state-dependent response. At fixed $\lambda$, varying $W$ yields two distinct delocalization windows, whereas varying $\lambda$ at fixed $W$ produces a single re-entrant delocalization window. These regimes arise within selected eigenstate sectors, where localized states coexist with extended or critical states, leading to mobility-edge-like behavior. The corresponding suppression of the Lyapunov exponent and enhancement of the dynamical RMS spreading are consistent with the IPR, NPR, and $D_2$ results. Finite-size scaling confirms the persistence of the re-entrant features, while the complex-energy spectrum resolves their state-selective structure. The resulting phase boundaries delineate distinct localization regimes in the $(W,\lambda)$ plane. Our results show that the interplay between quasiperiodicity and a staggered non-Hermitian modulation sharing the same quasiperiodic spatial structure can generate re-entrant, state-dependent localization, with implications for localization and dynamics in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices.
item.dc:creator: Souvik Roy, Santanu K. Maiti

item.title: Madelung hydrodynamics of spin-orbit coupling: action principles, currents, and correlations
item.description: arXiv:2601.10698v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We exploit the variational and Hamiltonian structures of quantum hydrodynamics with spin to unfold the correlation and torque mechanisms accompanying spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in electronic motion. Using Hamilton's action principle for the Pauli equation, we isolate SOC-induced quantum forces that act on the orbital Madelung--Bohm trajectories and complement the usual force terms known to appear in quantum hydrodynamics with spin. While the latter spin-hydrodynamic forces relate to the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), SOC-induced orbital forces originate from a particular current operator that contributes prominently to the spin current. This distinction between force terms reveals two fundamentally different mechanisms generating quantum spin-orbit correlations. Leveraging the Hamiltonian structure of the hydrodynamic system, we also elucidate spin transport features such as the correlation-induced quantum torques and the current shift in the spin Hall effect. This Hall shift leads to a new definition of the transport spin current thereby addressing an open question in spintronics. Finally, we illustrate the framework via the Madelung--Rashba equations for planar SOC configurations and propose a particle closure for possible numerical implementations.
item.dc:creator: Cesare Tronci

item.title: Anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping of thickness-quantized magnons
item.description: arXiv:2609.39612v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Magnon damping is a key factor governing spin-wave transport and nonlinear dynamics of multimode magnon systems. However, many descriptions rely on the assumption of an effective mode-independent parameter, which can mask wavelength-dependent relaxation processes that depend on propagation geometry and mode profile. Here, we employ high-resolution parametric-instability spectroscopy to probe thickness-quantized spin waves with wavelengths down to about a hundred nanometers in micrometer-thick yttrium iron garnet films. The instability threshold exhibits a regular sawtooth dependence on the magnetic field, arising from switching between discrete thickness modes. Comparison with dipole--exchange theory reveals anisotropic wavevector-dependent damping that increases with mode number and depends differently on the in-plane and out-of-plane wavevector components.
item.dc:creator: Tamara Azevedo, Rostyslav O. Serha, Yannik Kunz, Matthias R. Schweizer, Vitaliy I. Vasyuchka, Mathias Weiler, Andrii V. Chumak, Burkard Hillebrands, Mikhail Kostylev, Alexander A. Serga

item.title: Making Weak Interlayer Excitons Absorb via Purcell Engineering of Critical Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.20307v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Interlayer excitons (IXs) in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers possess unique dipolar properties, providing a path for exploring correlated many-body phases, electrically tunable dipole-dipole interactions, and long-range exciton transport. However, the large electron-hole separation underlying their dipolar character also results in a significantly reduced oscillator strength, limiting their direct optical interaction with light, and thus the direct probing of their dynamics and many-body interactions. Here, we show that by using Purcell engineering of critical coupling, a weak interlayer transition can absorb as strongly as the dominant intralayer transition, despite its much smaller intrinsic oscillator strength. Using this approach, in an open cavity architecture we demonstrate an order of magnitude IX absorption modulation in bilayer and trilayer MoS2, with doubling of the IX to A-exciton interaction strength weight from ~23% to ~53%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that in a tailored closed cavity architecture, the IX enhancement can reach beyond an order of magnitude, from ~5% to ~83% excitonic absorption, enabling IX absorption similar to intralayer excitons. An analytical description of the interaction is obtained via a closed-form transmission-line model which separates the excitonic and photonic contributions to the optical response, revealing how cavity architecture can be designed towards critical coupling. Our findings establish Purcell engineering of critical coupling as a general route to controlling and enhancing weak excitonic transitions.
item.dc:creator: Saroj Poudyal, Anabel Atash Kahlon, Michael Klein, Matan Meshulam, Yonatan Gershuni, Thomas Poirier, James H. Edgar, Mukesh Kumar, Seth Ariel Tongay, Itai Epstein
